title: Audit evidence escrow workflow and customer-triggered legal-hold API
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce an audit evidence escrow workflow and a customer-facing legal-hold API to guarantee tamper-evident admin/action logs, satisfy cross-region residency constraints, and support on-demand evidence exports for compliance requests. This ticket implements the orchestration layer that bundles signed WORM manifests, verifies storage integrity, and exposes controlled exports and retention overrides for customers with approved legal holds.
background: Customers in regulated industries have asked for two capabilities: (1) the ability to place an explicit legal hold on a tenant so that retention policies cannot delete audit evidence until release, and (2) an auditable escrow process that periodically snapshots sealed audit bundles to an external escrow storage location for long-term retention and regulator review. Current audit capture exists but lacks an integrated legal-hold API, escrow orchestration, and signed integrity manifests suitable for external verification.
proposed_solution: Add a Legal-Hold API endpoint on the Admin Console and Admin API that accepts a hold token, scope (tenant or project), reason, and expiry (optional). When a legal hold is active the retention enforcer will skip deletions for all audit evidence in scope. Implement an Escrow Orchestrator that: (a) periodically packages sealed WORM audit chunks into time-partitioned archives, (b) computes a digital manifest (SHA-256 + HSM-signed digest), (c) pushes the archive and manifest to configured escrow targets (S3 with Object Lock + external archival partners), and (d) records a notarized transaction in the immutable ledger. Provide verification tooling (CLI + SDK) that can fetch escrowed manifests and validate signatures and checksums against the ledger. Expose administrative events in Console with links to escrow receipts.
acceptance_criteria: API: Create/Release legal hold via Admin API; hold prevents deletion by retention enforcer and is visible in Console
Escrow: Orchestrator can produce time-partitioned audit bundles with accompanying signed manifests
Integrity: Each escrow bundle includes a manifest signed by HSM/KMS; verification CLI validates signature and checksums against ledger entry
Residency: Escrow targets support region constraints; bundles can be routed to region-local escrow buckets per customer config
Automation: Scheduled escrow runs succeed at scale for 100k audit events/day and emit receipts to Console and customer webhook
Docs & Controls: Runbook for legal team and ops, plus security review and threat model completed
design_notes: WORM storage will rely on S3 Object Lock in governance mode for hosted escrow targets and a signed manifest pattern for external partners. Use the existing immutable ledger component as the single source-of-truth for notarization; extend ledger entries with escrow_metadata fields (manifest_hash, escrow_target, timestamp, signature_ref). The Legal-Hold API will require RBAC scoping: only tenant admins or approved security roles can set/release holds. Holds must be auditable and emit a distinct audit action that is itself included in escrow bundles.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha - implement API + orchestrator with local dev-only escrow target; run end-to-end tests
Phase 2: Beta for select customers - enable region-aware escrow to S3 Object Lock buckets; gather feedback
Phase 3: GA - enable UI in Console, documentation, and partner escrow connectors; security review and customer migration guidance
test_plan: Unit tests for legal-hold enforcement paths and retention enforcer bypass logic
Load tests with synthetic audit streams at multiple scales to validate orchestrator throughput
Integration test: produce escrow bundle, verify manifest signature via HSM, validate ledger entry
Chaos test: simulate missing escrow target and validate retry/backoff and operator alerting
E2E: customer-facing SDK verifies manifests and performs a sample restore/inspection
risks: Operational complexity: escrow orchestration adds another persistent pipeline and failure modes
Cost: long-term external escrow storage may increase customer or Redwood costs; need pricing model
Security: signing keys require strict HSM policies and rotation procedures
Latency: creating signed manifests for very large bundles could add time to escrow windows
Compliance: cross-region escrow requires careful mapping to customer residency requirements
